content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text addresses whether the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row was answered or remains unresolved, which is the unanswered-witness counting situation K-G4 governs.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it': (1) acknowledging the row was answered and ruling UNDERDETERMINED does not count the verse as an unanswered witness; (2) treating that acknowledged answer as still an unresolved witness toward a broken link would count it.","why":"The judge expressly says CR2 and CR3 answered the loins/seed row and resolves the issue as UNDERDETERMINED rather than a broken link, so it does not count the answered verse as an unanswered witness."}
